content: The protein GGA1, also known as ADP-ribosylation factor-binding protein GGA1, is encoded by the GGA1 gene in humans. This gene produces a protein that belongs to the family of Golgi-localized, gamma adaptin ear-containing, ARF-binding (GGA) proteins. Members of this protein family are coat proteins that are ubiquitously expressed and play a critical role in regulating the trafficking of proteins between the trans-Golgi network and lysosomes. GGA1 proteins possess an amino-terminal VHS domain, which is essential for sorting mannose 6-phosphate receptors at the trans-Golgi network. Additionally, these proteins contain a carboxy-terminal region that shares homology with the ear domain of gamma-adaptins. This structural feature is significant for their functional interactions. The GGA1 gene undergoes alternative splicing, resulting in multiple transcript variants that encode different isoforms of the protein. These isoforms may have distinct functional roles in cellular processes. GGA1 has been experimentally demonstrated to interact with several other proteins, including Sortilin 1, BACE2 (Beta-site APP-cleaving enzyme 2), RABEP1 (Rabaptin-5), and ARF3 (ADP-ribosylation factor 3). These interactions suggest that GGA1 is involved in complex protein trafficking and sorting mechanisms within the cell.
